records.assertion: Brands Hatch hosted the 1986 British Grand Prix and Nigel Mansell won it.
records.notes: F1DB 1986 British GP at brands-hatch, winner Mansell.

records.assertion: Evaluative: Brands Hatch's elevation changes make it feel unlike a flat airfield circuit.
records.uk_issue: UK adds 'among the Kent hills' (location not in EN) and drops 'not simply another venue' and 'airfield'.
issues: no_checkable_fact
cited F1DB results file does not address topography
records.notes: Only source is a race-results YAML; nothing about elevation or character.

records.assertion: Mansell's first start at the 1986 British GP ended almost immediately when his car failed.
issues: figurative wording; read in context (he later won the restarted race)
records.notes: Figurative lead-in; factual core (failure at the start) supported by two sources.

records.assertion: Mansell's Williams stopped at the first start because of a broken CV (driveshaft) joint.
issues: source says 'drive shaft joint'; 'CV joint' is narrower wording not stated verbatim
records.notes: Grandprix.com only says the car 'failed'. Consider using the source's 'driveshaft joint' wording.

records.assertion: The race was red-flagged because of a crash behind Mansell, giving him a restart; the crash seriously affected another driver.
Mansell used the spare Williams, set up for Piquet, for the restart.
records.notes: Grandprix.com also: 'Mansell (in the spare car)'.

records.assertion: Jacques Laffite suffered severe leg injuries in the start crash, ending his F1 career.
records.notes: Sources also note a fractured pelvis.

records.assertion: Piquet led after the restart; Mansell passed him on lap 23 after Piquet missed a gear.

evidence.locator: race report, para 6 (same lap as Berger's lap-23 retirement)

issues: lap of pass: Grandprix.com implies lap 23, Motor Sport says lap 22
missed-gear cause only in Grandprix.com
records.notes: Piquet leading the restart is supported by both. Lap number conflicts between the two sources.

records.assertion: Pit stops did not decide the Williams battle; Mansell and Piquet finished 1-2 with Prost third, one lap down.
Mansell's win was a home win made possible by a restart caused by a crash (plus an editorial judgement).
issues: second clause is editorial/normative, not checkable
records.notes: Factual parts supported.

records.assertion: Evaluative: Brands Hatch is not a flat circuit.
issues: no_checkable_fact
records.notes: Source describes elevation at Paddock Hill but does not make the overall evaluation.

records.assertion: The GP loop dropped from Paddock Hill, climbed to Surtees, ran through woods, and returned to the main straight.
issues: 'climbed towards Surtees' not stated
source describes the modern layout, not the 1986 one
records.notes: Partly supported; climb to Surtees not established.

records.assertion: F1 raced at Brands Hatch on more than one layout, the last time in 1986.
issues: F1DB lists two layouts (brands-hatch-1 1964-74, brands-hatch-2 1976-86); 'several' may overstate
cited oversteer48 source does not cover F1 history
records.notes: Verified via F1DB layouts and race list (last race 1986).

records.assertion: The Dingle Dell chicane existed at the 1986 race; Sheene Curve was introduced in 2003.
issues: no date for Sheene Curve in cited source
no evidence the chicane existed in 1986
source calls Dingle Dell a 'corner', not a chicane
records.notes: ABC 2003 article (cited elsewhere) dates the Sheene Curve but not the chicane's 1986 status.

records.assertion: The 1986 GP lap had nine turns/sections (plus editorial caveat).
issues: F1DB gives turn count, not names; corner names for 1986 not sourced
editorial clause not checkable
records.notes: F1DB brands-hatch-2 (1976-86): 9 turns.

records.assertion: Mansell won the 1985 European GP at Brands Hatch for Williams, and it was his first WC win.
issues: 'first' World Championship win not established by cited source or package F1DB
records.notes: Win, venue and Williams supported; 'first win' is commonly reported but unsourced here.

records.assertion: Mansell started 3rd in 1985, behind pole-sitter Senna and second-placed Piquet.
issues: cited page is race result only; no grid positions
Mansell P3 and Piquet P2 not established
records.notes: Senna pole confirmed by F1DB. Grid order commonly reported; Lap Ledger (not cited here) lists Mansell winning from 3rd.

records.assertion: Mansell, often unlucky before, finally won a championship race (implying his first) at home.
records.uk_issue: UK says 'often unlucky' and 'won' without 'championship'; meaning roughly preserved.
issues: no_checkable_fact for 'near-misses'
'finally' (first win) and home nationality not in cited source
records.notes: Results page only.

records.assertion: The official 1985 European GP classification names Brands Hatch as the venue.
The 1986 British GP was the last WC F1 race held at Brands Hatch.
issues: 'last' rests on F1DB (no later brands-hatch race), not the cited page
records.notes: F1DB v2026.17.0 has no Brands Hatch race after 1986.

records.assertion: 1986: Piquet on pole; Mansell won over 75 laps; Piquet 2nd; Prost 3rd.
1986 was the final championship race at the Kent circuit, held before the 2003 Sheene Curve layout.
issues: cited results page mentions neither Kent nor Sheene Curve/2003
final-race part supported only by F1DB
records.notes: Sheene Curve 2003 is supported by the ABC source, which is cited for other claims but not this one.

records.assertion: Mansell set the fastest lap of the 1986 British GP.
issues: cited snapshot is the race-result tab and does not show fastest laps
records.notes: Verified via F1DB only.

records.assertion: Paddock Hill drops steeply from the start straight and is a right-hander.
issues: right-hand direction not stated in cited sources
records.notes: Drop supported; direction not.

records.assertion: Paddock Hill is named after the nearby paddock; braking downhill unsettles the car and compression at the bottom widens the exit.
issues: source describes modern driving, not 1986

records.assertion: The track climbs from Paddock Hill to Druids, a tight right-hand hairpin.
issues: right-hand direction not stated in cited sources
records.notes: Uphill hairpin supported; direction not.

records.assertion: The origin of the Druids name is uncertain/disputed.
records.notes: Source lists two druid-related theories.

records.assertion: A patient exit from Druids matters before the downhill section.
records.notes: Driving advice; source gives the same advice.

records.assertion: Graham Hill Bend is a left-hander dropping towards Cooper Straight, named after double champion Graham Hill.
issues: 'Cooper Straight' not mentioned in any cited source
records.notes: Name, direction and descent supported; Cooper Straight unsourced.

records.assertion: Graham Hill Bend's shape has changed since the F1 era.
Surtees is an uphill left-hander after which the GP circuit leaves the Indy circuit.
issues: 'climbing' not stated
split implied only by corner lists (GP: Hawthorn after Surtees; Indy: McLaren)
records.notes: Left-hander and split supported; climb not.

records.assertion: Surtees is named after John Surtees, world champion on motorcycles and in F1.
A clean Surtees exit sets up the faster wooded section that follows.
issues: no_checkable_fact

records.assertion: After descending Pilgrims Drop, Hawthorn Bend is a fast right-hander.
issues: 'Pilgrims Drop' not mentioned in any cited source
records.notes: Fast right-hander supported.

records.assertion: Sources disagree whether Hawthorn is named after Mike Hawthorn or a nearby farm.
records.notes: Same passage continues: other sources suggest a nearby farm.

records.assertion: Hawthorn's speed and camber make the approach unforgiving.
issues: camber not mentioned for Hawthorn
records.notes: Unforgiving/high speed supported; camber not.

records.assertion: Westfield is a quick right-hander named after nearby woodland.
issues: 'quick' not stated (source stresses it is tighter than Hawthorn)
right-hand direction only implied
records.notes: Name origin supported.

records.assertion: After Westfield the track drops to Dingle Dell; a wide exit compromised the old chicane that existed in 1986.
issues: no source establishes the chicane existed at the 1986 race
records.notes: Chicane replaced in 2003; its 1986 existence is undated in the sources.

records.assertion: In 1986 turn 7 was the original Dingle Dell chicane, not the Sheene Curve.
issues: 'not Sheene Curve in 1986' is supported (named 2003); 'chicane in 1986' not established
records.notes: Needs a period source (e.g. 1986 circuit map).

issues: article says curve 'recently been completed' by March 2003; construction may have begun in 2002

records.assertion: Evaluative: a modern turn-7 photo would misrepresent the historic corner.
